import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Define a logical order for customer age groups.
# This list should ideally cover all possible age groups that might appear in the dataset
# to ensure consistent sorting, even if some are not present in the current data.
full_age_group_order = ['<18', '18-24', '25-34', '35-44', '45-54', '55+', '65+']

# Aggregate data: calculate total sales for each product and customer age group
sales_by_product_age = df.groupby(['product', 'customer_age_group'])['total'].sum().unstack(fill_value=0)

# Get the unique age groups actually present in the dataset
actual_age_groups = df['customer_age_group'].unique()

# Filter and sort the actual age groups based on the predefined logical order
# This ensures that the age groups appear in a meaningful sequence on the plot.
sorted_age_groups = [group for group in full_age_group_order if group in actual_age_groups]

# Reindex the columns of the aggregated DataFrame to apply the sorted order
sales_by_product_age = sales_by_product_age.reindex(columns=sorted_age_groups)

# Set up the matplotlib figure
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 7))

# Create a heatmap to visualize total sales
sns.heatmap(
    sales_by_product_age,
    annot=True,        # Show the numerical values on the heatmap cells
    fmt=".0f",         # Format annotations as whole numbers (no decimal places)
    cmap="YlGnBu",     # Choose a sequential color map for better intensity representation
    linewidths=.5,     # Add lines between cells for better separation
    linecolor='white', # Color of the lines between cells
    cbar_kws={'label': 'Total Sales ($)'} # Label for the color bar legend
)

# Add title and labels for clarity
plt.title('Total Sales by Product and Customer Age Group', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Customer Age Group', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Product', fontsize=12)

# Rotate x-axis labels for better readability if they are long or numerous
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right')
# Ensure y-axis labels are horizontal
plt.yticks(rotation=0)

# Adjust layout to prevent labels/title from being cut off
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
